findings.F1: Outside the choppy profile, the tested stretch carries forward only in calm markets. findings.F2: In falling calm markets, a close below its 20-day average is followed by further fall. On the 10-day grid, the excess move in the short direction is +3.94 % for all closes below the average. For stretches beyond −1.5 swing units it is +5.49 % (36 cases), against +5.4 % of a usual 14.5 % move. In falling agitated markets the same deep-below cases give −1.01 % (52 cases), a small rebound rather than a continuation.

findings.F5: Rising calm continuation of the stretch is the strongest of these patterns. It reaches +6.18 % excess for closes above the average over 10 days and +6.58 % for stretches beyond +1.5 (47 cases). It repeats ideas the map already holds in rising calm (058-03.e1 calm rise stretch ten days, 035-01.b1, 058-02 range-edge continuation), so it is left out as already held.

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, the further a coin's close stands below its 20-day average, measured in units of its 20-day standard deviation of daily returns, the more the coin falls over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: In a calm decline, a close stretched far below its recent average is a reason to stay short or refuse a long, more so the larger the stretch.
ideas.name: falling calm stretch keeps falling

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the further a coin's close stands below its 20-day average, measured in units of its 20-day standard deviation of daily returns, the more the coin rebounds over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: In a swinging market, a deep stretch below the average is a reason to refuse a short, since the calm-market carry turns into a rebound there.
ideas.name: agitated stretch below rebounds
